sg.ra: Choose Center Orchestra rows C-G for one of the theater's best views at a desirable distance from the stage. For the most direct view in these rows, target center seats 107 to 114.

Rows H to L give a decent look at the stage for less than premium prices. Center Orchestra seats face more or less head-on to the stage, and stepped rows from J onward help keep rear sightlines clear.
Choose AA or BB for direct, sweeping overhead views of the stage.

sn.c: Legroom can get very cramped in the Mezzanine, with the best extra space on the aisles.
sn.sh: Mezzanine legroom can get very cramped

sn.c: Boxes elevated to the side offer private but slightly angled views.
sn.sh: Private but slightly angled box views

sn.c: There is a walkway in front of the edge seats in Orchestra row F for extra legroom.
sn.sh: Row F edge seats have extra legroom

sn.c: In the back rows, sightlines remain very good thanks to stepped rows kicking in at row J.
The Mezzanine overhang kicks in at row K, but isn’t an issue even in the very back seats.
In the Orchestra, the front four rows, C to G, are considered the best.
sn.sh: Front Orchestra rows are considered the best

sn.c: The best seats in the elevated Mezzanine can be found in rows AA to CC.
sn.sh: Best Mezzanine seats in rows AA to CC

vs.sum: A Roundabout Theatre Company house with excellent sightlines and good sound. Post-renovation seating is comfortable with decent legroom. Standout facilities include 30 women's restroom stalls — triple the building code requirement — virtually eliminating intermission lines.

acc.note: Elevator to all levels. 3 hearing loops. 100 Sennheiser hearing devices. 12 wheelchair seats.
